title: Review of lab 1 phase_membrane mature-damage repair (SIBR): repair to the undamaged twin within ~500 t on 2 of 3 new seeds; R by construction
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I looked at the claim's seed2 damage.png, then ran phase_membrane (unchanged, noise IC) with --damage rim 0.5 on new seeds 14 and 15 (frame 120) and 13 (frame 100; at frame 120 labkit fell back to an elongated 4.3x-median cell, so I moved the cut), plus same-seed undamaged twins (twin/seed13-15), and followed the same cell in the twin (twin_compare.py, twin_compare.png). Seed 14: a mature compact cell (age 23 frames, aspect 1.11) lost 24.9%; its wall closes by t=6250 and its area/pre goes 0.64 -> 1.02 at +10 frames against the twin's 1.04, and it then divides when the twin's cell does (+25-30 frames). Seed 15: 25.2% erased, 0.71 -> 1.49 at +10 frames against the twin's 1.53. Seed 13: 22.7% erased; the cut cell pinched into two by t=5850 and the followed piece stayed at 0.44-0.52 while the twin's cell was at 0.8-1.0, inconclusive. The link ring is present in all three reruns (radial L rim/core 1.75-1.83, rim/outside 3.9-5.0).

observations.S: rerun/seed14/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun/seed14/tracks.png: walled cells persist hundreds of frames between splits
observations.B: rerun/seed14/radial.png: L rim/core 1.75, rim/outside 4.98; the repaired target shows its bright wall again at t=6600 (rerun/seed14/damage.png)
observations.R: rerun/seed14/damage.png and twin_compare.png: 25% cut closes by t=6250, area 1.02 of pre-cut at +10 frames vs 1.04 for the same cell in twin/seed14; seed 15 1.49 vs 1.53

seeds_run.result: inconclusive: target pinched into two right after the cut; the followed piece diverged from the twin

controls_run.R: twin/seed14, twin/seed15, twin/seed13 (same seed, undamaged) with twin_compare.json

verdicts.limitation: Repair is curvature flow plus tilt, automatic by construction (so R is recorded, not scored, unless a mechanism finding shows it does work). Cells grow continuously and divide every ~1500 t, so 'mature, non-dividing' holds only for a window: both successful targets divided ~1300-1500 t after the cut, as their twins did. Erased fractions are 23-25%, not the 41% of the claim's seed 2. Twin areas are component-only (twin_compare.py) while labkit's damaged follow-up includes enclosed holes, so the ratios compare shapes of curves, not exact areas.
